messages.body_plain:
Hi anonymous,

I have now had a look, the first page is missing, because GGIR only adds a first page if all of the following conditions are met:
Argument dofirstpage is set to TRUE
There is valid entries of mean acceleration in part2 day summary for more than 1 day
There is a valid entry for MVPA in part 2 day summary for more than 1 day
The is more than 1 row of sleep in the night summary report.

In your case the part2 day summary only provides 1 day of data.

I think I implemented it this way to avoid having to deal with recordings with 1 or less days of data in the first page of the visual report. Ideally we want two valid days and nights to say something meaningful about a person's behaviour?

So, I am unsure whether this is a real problem that needs addressing by allowing for these days to be displayed and/or a warning to be shown.

Either way, it would take time to do this, so:
I welcome you or others to work on this.
If not possible, I'd be happy to work on this as a paid consultancy.

Thanks,

Vincent

However, I think your question is whether 3 days is enough to answer your research question. This depends on your research question, the sample size, the population you are studying and their typical day-to-day variation in behaviour, and the statistical analysis you intend to use.

This is probably not a GGIR discussion. So, I think you are better off looking up how studies in your field motivated their participant inclusion criteria and/or contacting researchers.

Best regards,

messages.body_plain:
> I wonder if any one received this error "recalibration not done because not enough points on all sides of the sphere" before. And what does it mean? I searched the GGIR documentation but I am still very confused. It would be great if anyone know about it can share the thoughts with me.

It means that the autocalibration algorithm did not have had enough data points to optimise the calibration. Typically this indicates that the recording is either too short or the accelerometer has hardly been worn throughout the recording. It is probably wise to exclude recordings from your analysis if any of the following conditions is met: calibration error is above 0.02, recording duration is less than a day, and/or accelerometer is not worn for more than a day.

> In addition,  I wonder in what case the files can not be process to part 2. I have about 73 files, but only get 67 files processed to part 2 when I run mode (1:2). I did not receive any error messages about it. Why will this happen?
​

Recordings that do not end up in the part 2 report, should be shown in the data quality report (QC folder), with a clarification why they were not processed such as file corrupt, file too short. Also, check that part2_daysummary.csv report which should clarify the amount of valid data per day. If this is below the set criteria then those days cannot be used for the person level aggregate.

Hi Sarah,

In case any of the following is helpful:
I used custom code: https://github.com/wadpac/psg-ncl-acc-spt-detection-eval tailored to the specific data sets I used for that study. The README <https://github.com/wadpac/psg-ncl-acc-spt-detection-eval/blob/master/README.md> file describes the key steps.
If your aim is to only evaluate sleep/wake classification without identification of the SPT window then the addition of simulated data is probably not necessary, because this classification is done per epoch and does not rely on algorithms to identify the largest episode of inactivity in a day.
If you want to include SPT window detection then the addition of artificial data may be done at two levels:
raw: Export data to csv file and append synthetic data to start and end, next process the csv files with GGIR.
epoch evel data: Go to GGIR part 1 output and append synthetic data to start and end.

Best,
Vincent

messages.body_plain:
Hi Alex,

GGIR intentionally starts at an integer number of large epochs (default length is 15 minutes) relative to the hour to ease interpretation and comparison of results across recordings and to ensure that epochs never span two different calendar dates. So, if your recording was started at 8:54:00 then you will see GGIR time series output from 9:00:00 onward. The first short (5 second) epoch will be from 9:00:00 and 9:00:05.

read.gt3x is a package that helps you read in the file directly but leaves it up to you to take care of all the data processing and alignment to compare individuals. This is where the value of GGIR comes in.

GGIR is designed for processing multi-day accelerometer data and because of that I think ignoring a few minutes at the beginning and end is justifiable.

Kind regards,
Vincent
